beats.narration: It's midnight. You're staring at the ceiling, and your brain is replaying that one awkward three-second mistake, again and again.
You're sure everyone in that meeting saw it and judged you for it. But cognitive science says you're dead wrong.
Here's the proof. In a Cornell study, students wore an embarrassing T-shirt into a room and guessed half the people would notice. Only 23 percent did.
That gap has a name: the spotlight effect. Inside your head, your flaws play at full volume, while everyone else is busy under their own spotlight.
So stop replaying it. Nobody has time to obsess over your small mistakes. The room moved on hours ago, and so can you.
